exposure: maternal age (younger adolescents aged <16 vs. older adolescents aged 16-19)
cohort: The study included 333 women with singleton pregnancies aged under 19 years at the time of delivery, who delivered at Hanoi Obstetrics and Gynecology Hospital.
finding: 84.7% of adolescent pregnancies experienced at least one maternal or neonatal adverse outcome, and younger adolescents (<16 years) were at higher risk for maternal anemia, threatened abortion, and urinary tract infection compared to older adolescents (16-19 years).
mod_finding: 41.4% of adolescent pregnancies resulted in cesarean delivery.
